original_value: The transport sector is commonly subordinate to several issues, such as traffic congestion and accidents. Despite this, in recent years, it is also evolving with regard to cooperation between vehicles. The fundamental objective of this trend is to increase road safety, attempting to anticipate the circumstances of potential danger. Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V), Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I) and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) technologies strive to give communication models that can be employed by vehicles in different application contexts. The resulting infrastructure is an ad-hoc mesh network whose nodes are not only vehicles but also all mobile devices equipped with wireless modules. The interaction between the multiple connected entities consists of information exchange through the adoption of suitable communication protocols. The main aim of the review carried out in this paper is to examine and assess the most relevant systems, applications, and communication protocols that will distinguish the future road infrastructures used by vehicles. The results of the investigation reveal the real benefits that technological cooperation can involve in road safety.

result.paraphrase: The transport sector is commonly burdened by problems such as traffic congestion and accidents. Even so, it has recently been advancing in terms of cooperation between vehicles. The main goal of this development is to improve road safety by trying to anticipate potential dangerous situations. Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V), Vehicle-to-Infrastructure (V2I), and Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) technologies aim to provide communication models that vehicles can use in different application contexts. The infrastructure that emerges is an ad-hoc mesh network whose nodes include not only vehicles but also all mobile devices equipped with wireless modules. Interaction among the various connected entities is based on exchanging information using appropriate communication protocols. The review in this paper primarily seeks to examine and evaluate the most relevant systems, applications, and communication protocols that will define the future road infrastructures used by vehicles. The findings show the real benefits that technological cooperation can bring to road safety.
